newsitem.title: USA: NYS Assembly says reaches pact on NYC tax levy.
newsitem.headline: NYS Assembly says reaches pact on NYC tax levy.

text.p: The New York State Assembly, which Gov George Pataki said was holding up a pact to extend New York City's 12.5 percent personal income tax, on Tuesday said that it had reached an agreement with all the parties.

"This agreement keeps cops on the streets and helps maintain our efforts to improve the conditions of our city's schools," said Sheldon Silver, D-Manhattan, who is the Assembly Speaker, in prepared remarks.

The pact, which still must be voted on by the Assembly, which is led by Democrats, and the Republican-controlled Senate, requires the city to keep the police force within two percent of the 38,310 level set in the legislation that first was approved in 1991. Failure to do so would incur penalities.

Gov George Pataki has signaled his support for the measure, which also was backed by New York City Mayor Rudolph Guiliani, who praised Silver for acting above partisan politics and added he was pleased by the measure. The New York City Council on Monday approved a matching bill.
State Senate Majority Leader Joseph Bruno, R-Troy, noted that the agreement obliged the city to hire a new class of police officers before June 30 to offset attrition.

Under the agreement, New York City would be forced to live up to its four-year capital plan, which calls for allocating $972 million for fiscal 1997 and 1998 towards school construction, plus another $550 million for supplemental capital.
The levy, expired at the end of 1996, would be extended until the end of 1998.

It would raise a projected $925 million of revenues in 1997 and 1998, and $650 million of this amount would help support the city's supplemental school capital program, with at least $275 million earmarked for police manpower and other criminal justice measures, Silver said in his release.
